record.paper_title: Some open problems in spectral theory
record.original_question: Let H be a Hilbert space, let A be a closed densely defined self-adjoint operator on H, and let (L_k) be a sequence of finite-dimensional closed subspaces of Dom(A) whose orthogonal projections P_k converge strongly to the identity operator. If Spec(A,L_k) denotes the spectrum of the finite-dimensional compression P_k A: L_k -> L_k, does Spec(A,L_k) converge to Spec(A), in an appropriate limiting sense, as k -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Projection methods: Let (Lk )k∈N be a sequence of closed linear (finite dimensional) subspaces of Dom(A) such that the corresponding orthogonal projections Pk : H → Lk converge strongly to the identity operator I. Let Λ(A) be the set of all such sequences of subspaces.
Does lim k→∞ Spec(A,Lk ) = Spec(A) hold for self-adjoint operators?
Does lim k→∞ Spec(A,Lk ) = Spec(A) hold for self-adjoint operators? No!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be a closed, densely defined, self-adjoint operator on $H$ with domain $\mathrm{Dom}(A)$ and spectrum $\mathrm{Spec}(A) \subset \mathbb{R}$. Let $(L_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of finite-dimensional closed subspaces with $L_k \subset \mathrm{Dom}(A)$, and let $P_k : H \to L_k$ be the orthogonal projection onto $L_k$. Assume that $P_k \to I$ strongly as $k \to \infty$. Define the finite-dimensional compression $A_k := P_k A\big|_{L_k} : L_k \to L_k$, and let $\mathrm{Spec}(A, L_k) := \mathrm{Spec}(A_k) \subset \mathbb{R}$.

Question: Does one always have, for every such $A$ and every such sequence $(L_k)$,
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} \mathrm{Spec}(A, L_k) = \mathrm{Spec}(A) $$
in the sense that the set-theoretic limit (e.g., Hausdorff limit on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}$) of $\mathrm{Spec}(A, L_k)$ equals $\mathrm{Spec}(A)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The answer is known to be negative in general: the Galerkin (projection) method applied to a self-adjoint operator can produce so-called "spectral pollution" — limit points of $\mathrm{Spec}(A, L_k)$ that lie in gaps of the essential spectrum of $A$ but do not belong to $\mathrm{Spec}(A)$. This is well documented in the literature on spectral pollution and motivates a variety of pollution-free schemes.

status_evidence.title: Spectral Pollution and How to Avoid It (Lewin–Séré)
status_evidence.snippet: The Galerkin method may fail dramatically when applied to eigenvalues in gaps of the essential spectrum, leading to spurious eigenvalues called spectral pollution.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Galerkin/projection approximation of a self-adjoint operator does not in general converge to its spectrum due to spectral pollution.

status_evidence.title: Generalised Weyl theorems and spectral pollution in the Galerkin method
status_evidence.snippet: Results identify the limiting set of spectral pollution arising from applying the Galerkin method to self-adjoint operators.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral pollution occurs and has been characterized for self-adjoint operators under projection methods.
